types.name: ScrollRevealProps
types.doc: Animates its children in as the wrapper scrolls into view. Each direct child becomes one step of the sequence, so a list, a grid or a row of cards arrives one after another. Pair it with `ScrollProgress` to show how far the reader is.

members.name: children
members.doc: Each direct child is revealed as one step.

members.name: effect
members.doc: How the children arrive: a plain fade, a slide from one side, a scale up, or a blur that comes into focus.

members.name: from
members.doc: The side the "slide" effect comes from.

members.name: distance
members.doc: Distance in px that the "slide" effect travels.

members.name: stagger
members.doc: Seconds between one child and the next. Use 0 to reveal them together.

members.name: delay
members.doc: Seconds to wait before the first child starts.

members.name: once
members.doc: True reveals once and keeps the result; false hides the children again when they leave and replays on every entry.

members.name: amount
members.doc: How much of the wrapper must be visible before it starts, from 0 to 1.

members.name: root
members.doc: The scrolling element to watch. Leave it out when the page itself scrolls.

members.name: className
members.doc: Extra class for the wrapper, for example a grid or a flex row.

members.name: itemClassName
members.doc: Extra class for the element wrapped around each child.

members.name: container
members.doc: The scrolling element to measure. Leave it out to follow the page.

members.name: label
members.doc: Accessible name of the progress bar.

members.name: position
members.doc: "sticky" stays at the top of its scroll container, "fixed" pins to the top of the window, "static" stays where it is rendered.
